prize_parts.citation: For experimental demonstration and quantitative mapping of long-range electron tunnelling through proteins

statement.case_for: B023 is the only shortlisted candidacy that states a biological mechanism in physical terms and rests on a clearly attributable experimental discovery. Photo-triggered kinetics in ruthenium-modified proteins showed that electron-transfer rates fall off with distance and depend on the intervening protein structure, and that multistep hopping extends the reach. This underlies respiratory and photosynthetic energy conversion, including the enzymes I work on. The result has been confirmed over roughly four decades in many proteins and laboratories, so maturity is not in question. The credited pair is compact and fits a two-person prize without crowding the three-laureate limit. My ranking is a statement about the science, not a count of opening votes.
statement.case_against: Opening support is thin: no colleague except me ranked B023 at all, so my first place cannot be treated as committee evidence. The 1992 prize to Marcus already honoured the theory of electron transfer, and some members may see the field as covered. Dutton and Moser, Beratan and Onuchic, and others on natural enzymes may have priority claims the credited pair does not resolve. I have a disciplinary affinity for this work, and I discount my own enthusiasm accordingly. If the expert report places Gray and Winkler's contribution as an extension of Marcus theory rather than a discovery, B057 is the strongest alternative on maturity and attribution.

responses.point: Johan calls massively parallel sequencing (B057) a true game-changer, a chemistry solution of nucleotide design, surface chemistry and fluorescence detection, and would honour the Cambridge chemistry rather than the commercial platforms.
responses.response: I agree on maturity and impact, and the Balasubramanian-Klenerman core is a clean pair. My reservation is the one Heiner raised: the field was already honoured near this area in 1980 (Gilbert and Sanger), and the Rothberg, Ju and Mayer claims make priority commercially entangled. Whether it is a chemical discovery or an enabling technology should be settled by the expert report. I place it as my first alternative, not my first choice.

responses.point: Andrei ranks targeted protein degradation (B066) first as a clear, general design principle with confirmed mechanism, a trio of Crews, Deshaies and Handa, and recognition that looks timely.
responses.response: The principle of induced proximity is well confirmed, and I do not dispute its originality. I disagree on timing and attribution. No degrader drug is yet approved, which Daniel, Emma and Johan also noted, and the three-name trio splits a PROTAC strand and a cereblon-glue strand, leaving out Ciulli, Gray, Sakamoto, Kim and Ito. That is a priority problem the three-laureate limit cannot absorb cleanly. I would hold B066 for a later year unless the report shows the two strands converge on one attributable discovery.

responses.point: Emma ranks biomolecular phase separation (B036) first as a general physical-chemical principle for membrane-free organisation, with Hyman, Brangwynne and Rosen as the most defensible trio.
responses.response: I share the appeal of a physical description, and I ranked B036 fourth myself. But the in vitro to in vivo question is not a side issue: some condensate claims depend on artefact-prone assays and have not held up, so the mechanism in cells is less settled than the concept. Pappu and Mittag are also left out of the trio. I would want the expert report to separate the established physics from the contested biology before supporting it as the lead part.

responses.point: Heiner, as chair, puts halide perovskite solar absorbers (B068) first for a clear physical basis and a new materials capability, while noting that credit among six names and near-simultaneous 2012 results makes any trio contestable.
responses.response: Heiner's own attribution caveat is the decisive point for me. The first perovskite-sensitised cell, the solid-state step change and the thin-film architecture came from different groups within months of each other, so any three-name selection is a priority judgement the record may not support. Stability and lead toxicity also remain open. I would need the expert report to show a defensible trio before moving it above candidates with cleaner credit.

responses.point: Peter Somfai ranks Pd-catalysed C-N coupling (B038) first: general, mechanistically understood, with a clean two-person prize for Buchwald and Hartwig, and distinct from the 2010 cross-coupling prize.
responses.response: Attribution is indeed the cleanest on the table, and I accept the thirty years of confirmation. My qualification is scope: it is a refinement of a methodology honoured in 2010, which Johan and Xiaodong also raised, and I weigh a new fundamental mechanism above an extension of an existing one. I do not rule it out and would treat it as a serious option if the report judges the C-N step to be a distinct achievement.

uncertainties: Whether the expert report treats Gray and Winkler's experiments as a discovery distinct from Marcus theory (1992 prize) and from Dutton-Moser and Beratan-Onuchic work
Whether B057 sequencing is judged a chemical discovery rather than an enabling technology, and how to resolve Rothberg, Ju and Mayer priority
How the committee weighs approval-pending clinical status for B066 and the contested in vivo relevance for B036
statement.conflict_note: No specific conflict is apparent from my profile for any shortlisted candidate. I note that Xiaodong Zou is a Stockholm University colleague, and that I have a field affinity with B023 through bioenergetics and electron transfer, but I have no personal or institutional tie to Gray or Winkler. The committee should be aware of that affinity when weighing my ranking.
